sections.overview: Paucidentomys vermidax is a highly specialized shrew-rat known from the mountains of Sulawesi, Indonesia.
sections.identification: Its long snout ends in unusual bicuspid upper incisors; it has no molars.
sections.habitat: Records come from montane forest on Mount Latimojong and the transition between lowland and montane forest on Mount Gandangdewata, in high-elevation habitat above about fifteen hundred metres.
sections.diet: One examined stomach contained earthworm segments and no other food; the authors therefore proposed that it may specialize on earthworms and other soft-bodied prey.
sections.behavior: Its teeth appear adapted to cut or tear soft prey before swallowing rather than to gnaw or grind, but direct behavioral observations remain sparse.
sections.reproduction: The original description did not establish its breeding season, litter size or nesting behavior.
sections.ecology: The authors compare it with Rhynchomys, an ecologically similar shrew-rat from Luzon. A 2025 Indonesian survey examined local occurrence and knowledge around Gandang Dewata, but did not estimate abundance.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports the IUCN category Near Threatened; the very small known range and limited records make further survey valuable.
